# hands/people

who Teeny talks to, what they asked, what it promised.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/people <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): promise; kept, drop
- Job (writes state or calls the core): none
- Operator only (never call): forget SURFACE WHO
- Read only: list [--all]; get SURFACE WHO

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `list [--all]` | R | Regulars, and anyone with an open promise, most recent first: messages, days, first and last, open promises, requests. |
| `get SURFACE WHO` | R | One record: the counts, the opening of their last 3 messages (200 characters each), what they asked to build, and every promise (made, due, status, `overdue`). |
| `promise` | A | `{surface, who, what, due_in_hours \| due_at, ref?}`, due within 90 days. |
| `kept` / `drop` | A | `{id, note?}`: an open promise kept or dropped; its follow-up is cleared if it still waits. |
| `forget SURFACE WHO` | O | A person asked to be forgotten: their promises and follow-ups go. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `drop`, `forget`, `get`, `kept`, `list`, `promise`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--all`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `DRY_RUN=1 hands/people <verb> --help`. The full account is in docs/hands.md.
